To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the president's cabinet appointments are a function of the president's political ideology and his party affiliation, but not a function of his party's control of Congress or his party's strength in Congress.

(1) the president's choice of a cabinet reflects his view of the proper relationship between the executive and legislative branches of government; (2) the cabinet reflects the president's view of his role as a leader; (3) the president's cabinet choices reflect his view of the role that the president should play in the policy-making process; (4) the president's view about the proper role of the president is influenced by the political environment, the political party, and his personal background and experience.

(a) the president's cabinet appointments are not random, (b) the pattern of appointments is consistent across administrations, and (c) the pattern is related to the president's political ideology and to the political ideology of his party.
